correctness.rationale: The twenty explicit vertices and thirty minimum-length edges have exact algebraic coordinates. All ten antipodal great-circle normals and forty-five transverse intersection pairs were checked in Z[sqrt(5)]. Each spherical chamber must contain a pairwise circle corner, so enumerating four sign quadrants at each oriented intersection gives the complete 92-cell partition, not a statistical approximation. The exact sign table determines 20 hexagonal/section-6, 60 triangular/section-8 and 12 pentagonal/section-10 chambers. All internal angle multisets were computed exactly, then Girard spherical excess yields the claimed probabilities. A separate 30-edge angular-separation expectation confirms the law. The included actual checker reruns the finite exact certificate; generic continuum cases are exhausted by the proof.

originality.rationale: Actual exact-alias and dual-silhouette queries returned no coincident regular-dodecahedron Haar three-mass law. The closest published central-icosahedron section law has a different object and only two section counts; exact dodecahedral sections are polar to icosahedral shadows, not to central icosahedral sections. Direct inspection of the motivating arXiv full text found a general section-arrangement and reconstruction theory, without this 92-cell spherical area distribution. Full inspected Platonic projected-area variance and rectangular-box section laws concern distinct statistics/objects. The finite certificate computes nontrivial exact probabilities; older unindexed equivalent work remains possible.

value.rationale: The complete three-point Haar polygon-side distribution and its 92 exact spherical chamber classes form a natural and quantitatively nontrivial invariant of central sections of a canonical centrally symmetric Platonic solid, and via polarity of icosahedral silhouettes. Determining these area fractions is stronger than computing possible side counts, a general section-reconstruction principle, or shadow area variance. The result is motivated directly by current research on section-count functions and is a self-contained exact classification with geometric utility.
